title: Higher direct images preserve local quasi-coherence and flat comparison maps on algebraic stacks
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of algebraic stacks over $B$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Give each fibred category its big etale site (same objects and arrows as its big fppf site of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], with coverings the families lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps), and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(x)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $x$ over $U$. Let $F$ be a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on this site. Call $F$ locally quasi-coherent if for every object $x$ over $U$ its restriction to the small etale site $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] is the associated etale sheaf of a quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_x$ [pqf-def-coherent]; the associated sheaf on an etale $v:V\to U$ has sections $\Gamma(V,v^*F_x)$. For an arrow $a:x\to y$ over $u:U\to V$, let $c_a:u^*F_y\to F_x$ be the canonical comparison induced by restriction, with ordinary tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Say that $F$ has flat comparison maps if $c_a$ is an isomorphism whenever the underlying scheme map is flat; equivalently, on affine opens the corresponding ring maps are flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose $F$ is locally quasi-coherent and has flat comparison maps. Then $F$ is also an fppf sheaf. For every integer $i\geq0$, the higher direct image $R^if_*F$, formed by applying $f_*$ to an injective resolution in module sheaves and taking its $i$th cohomology sheaf, is locally quasi-coherent and has flat comparison maps on $\mathcal Y$. Computing in the big etale topology or the big fppf topology gives canonically the same result. Here on either site the direct image is the sheaf with value $(f_*F)(y)=\Gamma(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}U,F|_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}U})$ at $y:U\to\mathcal Y$; restriction to this fibre product is precomposition with its projection, and the restrictions of $f_*F$ are induced by the corresponding base-change maps. In degree zero $R^0f_*F=f_*F$, and its $c_a$ is the map induced by these restrictions. No Noetherian, finite-generation or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0765 (lemma-flat-comparison) and 0771 (proposition-loc-qcoh-flat-base-change), parts (1) and (4); definition-flat-base-change and section-locally-quasi-coherent specify the comparison maps and local quasi-coherence. Degree-zero direct image is the section definition, not an assertion of arbitrary-base-change quasi-coherence.

proof.text: For every algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/B$, let $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$ consist of the locally quasi-coherent sheaves with flat comparison maps. By [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-flat-comparison-local-structure] these subcategories are weak Serre, are preserved by smooth pullback, and have membership detected by jointly surjective smooth families. These are exactly conditions (1)--(3) of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-descent-higher-image-criterion]. We verify its affine condition (4) next; that verification concerns every morphism between affine schemes, not just the original $f$.

source.place: Tag 0765, proof, first paragraph; Tag 076Z, conditions (1)--(4).

proof.text: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of affine schemes regarded as stacks, with $M\in\mathcal M_X$. For any test $y:V\to Y$, put $Z=X\times_YV$, $a:Z\to V$, and $N=M|_{Z_{\mathrm{et}}}$. The map $a$ is affine: locally where $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}D$, its source is $\operatorname{Spec}(D\otimes_A C)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Its inverse image over each affine open of $V$ is affine and therefore quasi-compact. Its relative diagonal is closed: on these affine charts it is induced by the surjection $(D\otimes_A C)\otimes_C(D\otimes_A C)\to D\otimes_A C$, $r\otimes s\mapsto rs$. Hence $a$ is separated. Local quasi-coherence of $M$ says that $N$ is associated to a quasi-coherent Zariski module; [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] makes it quasi-coherent on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [lem-sfb-stack-representable-higher-image-restriction], $(R^ih_*M)|_{V_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq R^ia_*N$. The latter is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-higher-direct-image-quasi-coherent], and [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies it with an associated Zariski module. This proves local quasi-coherence for every $i$ in condition (4).

source.place: Tag 0765, affine case; proof of lemma-pushforward-locally-quasi-coherent; Tag 075P and Tag 0720.

proof.text: For a flat test arrow $b:V\to V^{\prime}$ over $Y$, put $Z^{\prime}=X\times_YV^{\prime}$, $Z=Z^{\prime}\times_{V^{\prime}}V$, and write $e:Z\to Z^{\prime}$, $a^{\prime}:Z^{\prime}\to V^{\prime}$ and $a:Z\to V$. The map $e$ is flat by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] (a scheme morphism is representable by algebraic spaces). Therefore the hypothesis on $M$ identifies $e^*(M|_{Z^{\prime}_{\mathrm{et}}})$ with $M|_{Z_{\mathrm{et}}}$. Under [lem-sfb-stack-representable-higher-image-restriction], the comparison for $R^ih_*M$ is the small-etale base-change morphism for $(a^{\prime},b)$ followed by the map on higher images of this coefficient identification. Thus it remains to check that specified base-change morphism, not merely existence of isomorphic source and target.

source.place: Tag 0765, affine case, the two cartesian squares and the final comparison map.

proof.text: For $i=0$, [lem-sfb-space-flat-direct-image-base-change] makes the specified small-etale base-change map an isomorphism: $a^{\prime}$ is affine, hence quasi-compact separated, $b$ is flat, and the coefficient is quasi-coherent as checked above. For $i>0$, [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-higher-image-vanishing] applied to the affine morphisms $a^{\prime}$ and $a$ says both their higher direct images are zero; their base-change map is consequently the unique map from zero to zero, hence an isomorphism. The coefficient identification in the preceding step is also an isomorphism. This verifies the flat comparison property in every degree for condition (4).

source.place: Tag 0765, affine case; spaces-cohomology.tex Tags 073K(1) in degree zero and 073H in positive degrees.

proof.text: All four hypotheses of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-descent-higher-image-criterion] now hold for the rule $\mathcal M$. Apply its conclusion to the given quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and the given $F\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal X}$. It gives $R^if_{\mathrm{et},*}F\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal Y}$ for every $i\geq0$. Thus the etale higher images are locally quasi-coherent and have the required comparison isomorphisms for every flat scheme arrow.

source.place: Tag 0765, application of Tag 076Z after the affine calculation.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-lfp-topology-comparison] hold for $F$: its comparison maps are isomorphisms for all flat arrows, in particular for flat locally finitely presented ones. It is therefore an fppf sheaf. Apply the same node also to each $G_i=R^if_{\mathrm{et},*}F$, using the properties proved in Step 5, to see that every $G_i$ is already an fppf sheaf. Finally that node identifies $R^if_{\mathrm{fppf},*}F$ with the fppf sheafification of $G_i$. Sheafification of an existing fppf sheaf is canonically that sheaf by its universal property. The identification uses the same underlying module presheaf and its restriction maps, so it preserves both the local quasi-coherent modules and their canonical $c_a$. This proves the asserted equality of the two topology computations.

source.place: Tag 0771, proof of (1) and (4); stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 075R(3).

proof.text: In degree zero take an injective resolution $0\to F\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$. The section formula for $f_*$ preserves kernels: a section is a compatible family and belonging to a kernel is checked at every object of the fibre site. Hence $\ker(f_*I^0\to f_*I^1)=f_*F$, so $R^0f_*F=f_*F$. This identifies the isomorphism with the specified section functor, whose comparison maps are induced by its original restriction maps, as required. No finiteness or Noetherian assumption was used in the argument.

source.place: Conventions on direct image, preceding section-pullback; degree-zero case of Tag 0771(4).
